intended_object: The functorial action on maps of the least fixed point (initial algebra) `Fix F` of a multivariate QPF F. Given g : α ⟹ β, it sends `Fix F α` to `Fix F β` by mapping g over the first n parameters while leaving the recursive argument alone. The object comes from the docstring "`Fix F` is a functor" and from its use as the `map` in the `MvFunctor (Fix F)` instance.
explanation: `Fix F α` is the quotient of the W-type `q.P.W α` by `WEquiv`. `Fix.map` lifts the W-type map `q.P.wMap g` to this quotient. The lemma `wEquiv_map` shows that `wMap` respects the equivalence, so the lift is well defined. This is the standard way to define the functor action on a quotient of W-types, and it is used directly as the `map` in the `MvFunctor (Fix F)` instance. It works for any n, any multivariate QPF F and any TypeVecs α and β, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no separate, more general version: this is Mathlib's own definition.
